english: A herdsman was driving the cows to the stream. The snow was melting, and the stream was big. At the ford a cow slipped. The herdsman went into the water. The current seized him, and he sank. english: Child, whose daughter are you? I am the daughter of a woman who died when I was born. Where is your father? The current carried him off at the ford. Who feeds you? A villager's wife feeds me, but her boys are many. At night I lie among the dogs. Come with me; my wife will feed you.

english: Mother Earth, we give you this mortal. And cover him with your hands. Do not give him to the dogs; guard him from the wolves. May he rest in you; may he not return home. Now we set a stone for him. And may his name not be lost.

english: There were two brothers, twins. There was no sky, and there was no sun. Then the one killed the other. From his flesh he made the earth. From his bones he made the stones. From his skull he made the sky. From his blood he made the waters. That was the first sacrifice. Now mortals kill bulls for the gods.

english: Mother-in-law, I saw my husband in a dream. What did he say to you? He said nothing. He stood at the door, and he was cold, and he was trembling. The dead are hungry if no one feeds them. english: A young bride was carrying a child in the womb. When the birth came, the women gathered in the house. In the night she suffered pain, and she called on the gods. At dawn a son was born. english: The path of the dead is long and dark. Two black dogs guard it. They let the good man go. They tear the lying man. Those whom no one laid in the earth do not reach the path. They walk among the houses in the darkness. So mortals lay the dead under stones.

english: The king left the dead man in the field for the dogs. No one covered him; all trembled before the king. Then his sister came in the darkness. With her hands she threw earth on him. She poured out water and milk, and she chanted for him. The dogs did not eat him. In the morning the king caught sight of it, and he raged.

english: Who lived in this house? My grandfather lived here with his kin. Who burned it? Enemies arrived in the night. They shut the door. The people were inside. Then they burned the house. How did you escape? I was among the sheep in the field, and I caught sight of the smoke. May the gods punish those enemies! The gods saw it, and they were silent.

english: Mother, what shall we do for father? We will wash him with warm water. Then we will clothe him in a white garment. Shall we cover him with stones? We will not cover him with stones; we will burn him. Fire will convey him to the gods. Where will his bones lie? His bones will lie under a stone, and the stone will protect them. I will groan with you.

english: Grandfather, why do we burn the dead? We burn them, and the smoke carries them to the sky. Where do the dead go? They go along the path of the dead, and two dogs guard it. Will the dogs let my father go? They will let him go; he was a good man. The dogs tear the wicked. Then I will be good.

english: Under the ford lives the water god. In summer he takes one man. He pulls him down by the feet. No one sees him. A young man did not tremble before the god. He went into the ford at night with his horse. In the morning the horse arrived home alone. The god took the young man and did not let him go. His mother searched for him at the ford for a year.
